note: Ninth and final round: re-tested case 4 against internal/run's fallbackTransport fix (commit 562ffd2), which was meant to let the orchestrator itself reach a broker/Prometheus dual-homed inside the DC-2-isolated stack, closing round 8's reachability finding. It does not, for a newly-diagnosed, more specific reason (see reachability_finding below) -- the standalone dual-homed workaround was restored and is still required. The corpus remains complete: all 8 cases built and measured, none faked or skipped.

case4_nonidempotent_consumer.defect: Non-idempotent consumer: applies its side effect (an in-memory counter increment) for every message it reads off a Redpanda topic, with no per-message dedup check at all.
case4_nonidempotent_consumer.fault: duplicate: 1.0 on target 'orders' (a topic name, not a host:port), at: peak for: 5s -- internal/queuefault's BrokerApplier, driving Redpanda's Pandaproxy (Kafka REST Proxy v2-compatible) over plain HTTP, exactly as internal/applier/broker_applier.go documents.
case4_nonidempotent_consumer.assert_form_used: promql: 'orders_processed_total <= orders_received_total' -- the ONLY assert form that could express this defect. k6 thresholds cannot see it at all: every POST /order still returns 202 whether or not the message is later processed twice, so no duration/failure-rate threshold would ever break. sql: reads as permanently unevaluated (no SQL execution path exists in v0, confirmed by reading internal/run/findings.go's evaluateSQLAsserts). promql: is fully evaluable given a live Prometheus and -prom-url -- confirmed by reading internal/run/findings.go's evaluatePromqlAsserts, which only reports 'not evaluated' when the querier is nil.
case4_nonidempotent_consumer.candidates_reason: Same structural gap as poison_pill/duplicate always hits: buildCandidates(fault, deps, lang) looks up depForTarget(deps, f.Target) by exact Dep.Address match, which is always host:port-shaped for every other fault verb -- but queuefault.Translate uses f.Target as a bare topic name (Topic: f.Target), which can never match a Dep.Address. This means D-9 candidates are structurally impossible for poison_pill/duplicate findings specifically, regardless of whether the underlying broker (Redpanda here, a recognized image type) is itself detected -- a narrower, more specific version of the case 1/2/5 gap. Reported, not patched (out of scope).
case4_nonidempotent_consumer.repeat_runs: 3/3 clean detections across repeat runs, confirming this isn't a fluke.

reachability_finding.title: fallbackTransport's tunnel dial target ("localhost") does not work against an IPv4-only listener, which Redpanda's Pandaproxy is
reachability_finding.severity: structural, still blocks -broker-url (and, by the same mechanism, -prom-url) against any IPv4-only-bound in-stack target -- a common default, not an edge case
reachability_finding.status: round 1 of this finding (round 8: BrokerApplier/HTTPPromQuerier had no join-the-namespace mechanism at all) is FIXED by commit 562ffd2's fallbackTransport. Round 2 (this round): the fix's own tunnel is broken for this exact case.
reachability_finding.detail: Re-ran case 4 with docker-compose-managed Redpanda/Prometheus (natural layout, no workaround) and -broker-url http://redpanda:8082 -prom-url http://prometheus:9090, per the coordinator's ask. Confirmed the direct-attempt-then-fallback logic itself fires correctly (the error changed from a plain 'connection refused' to 'EOF', and discoverSUTContainer("redpanda") does find the right container -- using "localhost" as the URL host, as first tried, gets 'connection refused' with no fallback at all, since discoverSUTContainer("localhost") finds no such compose service; using the real service name in the URL, "redpanda", is what triggers the tunnel). But the tunnel itself then fails every time with EOF. Reproduced directly, entirely outside TortureU: `docker run --network container:<redpanda-container-id> alpine:3.20 nc -v localhost 8082` fails deterministically (exit 1, no output) across 4 repeat attempts; the identical command with `127.0.0.1` instead of `localhost` succeeds every time ('127.0.0.1 (127.0.0.1:8082) open', exit 0). Redpanda's own /proc/net/tcp inside that netns shows its listener bound to 0.0.0.0 only (confirmed: local_address '00000000:1F92', no IPv6 entry at all). BusyBox nc (the image internal/run/inreach.go's containerNetDialer uses) resolves the bare hostname 'localhost' to ::1 first and does not fall back to the A record (127.0.0.1) when that connection is refused -- confirmed separately: connecting to '::1' directly also fails. containerNetDialer hardcodes the literal string "localhost" as its dial target; using "127.0.0.1" there would have worked for this case. Any real-world container image bound to 0.0.0.0 only (a very common default -- Redpanda is not unusual here) would hit this identically.
reachability_finding.workaround_still_required: evals/corpus/case4-nonidempotent-consumer/run.sh runs Redpanda and Prometheus as standalone containers this script manages directly (never declared in docker-compose.yml, so ComposeTopologyApplier's overlay never touches them), each on a dedicated user-defined bridge network with a host-published port. This is test-harness engineering to make a measurement possible, not evidence the underlying gap doesn't exist: a user running `tortureu run -broker-url http://redpanda:8082 ...` against their own plain docker-compose.yml -- exactly the documented, natural way to use this flag -- would hit the identical EOF this workaround exists to route around.

secondary_findings_from_building_this_fi: Pandaproxy's own auto-create-topic-on-first-produce path hung for 5+ seconds per attempt rather than failing fast or succeeding quickly, in this Redpanda version/config -- pre-creating the topic explicitly (via rpk) sidesteps it entirely. Not a TortureU defect (Redpanda's own behavior), but worth recording since it shaped the fixture.

config.Parse's fault-target validation (`knownTargets`) is purely syntactic -- built only from the SUT's own service name and torture.yaml's own declared egress.hosts keys, with no access to detect.System -- so a queue-fault's topic-shaped target has to be declared in egress.hosts even though internal/run's own queuefault routing never actually consults that classification for poison_pill/duplicate (unlike error_rate, which IS checked against class: mock). The declaration is required to pass the parser and then entirely inert. Not a bug -- config.Parse cannot see detect.System's output by design -- but a real rough edge for anyone writing a queue-fault torture.yaml.

metrics.detection: 7/7 planted defects detected (all cases 1-7 now built and measured). Case 8 (control) correctly found nothing. The corpus is complete.
metrics.attribution: 4/4 fault-driven cases (1, 2, 4, 5) named the correct causing fault exactly (Cause.fault and Cause.target both matched the planted fault). Cases 3, 6, 7 are load-only by design -- no fault exists to attribute, not counted as a hit or a miss.
metrics.candidates: 2/7 findings-bearing cases carry a candidate list: case 3 (pgx -- MaxConns, the exactly-right knob) and case 7 (go-redis, present and honestly caveated). Cases 1, 2, 4, 5 carry none -- three distinct, precisely diagnosed structural reasons, all reported rather than routed around: (a) a custom application image outside detect's closed vocabulary never becomes a detect.Dep (cases 1, 2, 5); (b) net/http can never be discovered as a client via manifest scanning regardless of vocabulary, since it's stdlib and never appears in a go.mod require line, and internal/detect's own recognition table has no net/http entry either (cases 1, 2, 5); (c) a queue-fault's topic-shaped target can never match a Dep.Address, which is always host:port-shaped (case 4). Case 6 correctly carries none (in-process queue, no client library exists to find).
metrics.false_positive_on_control: 0, across 20 consecutive case-8 runs spanning six different code-path states. Never non-zero once actually measured.
